labPage.entryHeading: How do you want to start?

goals.pc: Assemble a complete PC that passes its startup check.
goals.network: Connect two devices and get a packet from one to the other.

starts.pc: No experience needed. You begin by getting to know the main parts.
starts.network: No experience needed. You begin with what a cable, a switch and a router do.

next.none: Start in Learn mode. It goes step by step.
next.learn: Learn is selected. Guided lessons are not built yet, so for now it opens the workspace without steps.
next.free: Free Lab is selected. It has no fixed steps.
next.test: Test Yourself is selected. Checked challenges are not built yet, so for now it opens the workspace without checks.

action.pc: Name your build and press “Create build”. That opens the workspace.
action.network: Name your network and press “Create network”. That opens the workspace.

scene.heading: 3D view
scene.intro: Click a part to pick it up, then click a highlighted place. Cyan places can take it; amber ones cannot, and clicking one tells you why. Everything here can also be done in the list below. The camera stays where you leave it while you select and install parts. Move it yourself with the view controls, drag, or zoom.
scene.educational: Educational models, not manufacturer-accurate. A part with no model yet is drawn as an outline box of its size.
scene.unavailable: The 3D view can't start in this browser (no WebGL). The list below does everything the 3D view does.
scene.lost: The 3D view stopped (the graphics context was lost). The list below still works.
scene.failed: The 3D view ran into a problem and was closed. The list below still works.
scene.canvasLabel: 3D view of your build. Arrow keys turn the camera, plus and minus zoom.
scene.keys: With the picture focused: arrow keys turn the camera, + and − zoom. Drag with a mouse or finger to turn, scroll or pinch to zoom. Orbit stays centred on the workbench; dragging rotates the view without panning it away. Use Fit all to centre the current parts again.
scene.benchAssembly: Prepare the motherboard on the workbench first: CPU, RAM, M.2 drive and CPU cooler/block. Then select the motherboard and place it in the case; its attached parts move with it. Finish with the graphics card, power supply, case fans, radiator and cables. A SATA drive mounts in the case.

learning.name: Your Tech Lab
learning.tagline: Build your PC. Write your code. Find your way.
learning.intro: A place to try, learn, and make things work—with a little helper when you need one.
learning.helpStartDetail: A clear first step, a small example, then your turn.
learning.selfStartDetail: Choose a lab and try your ideas at your own pace.
learning.chooseTitle: What would you like to try?
learning.startSteps: 1. Choose code or PC assembly. 2. Try a small step. 3. Run it, then ask the helper if you get stuck.
learning.helperNote: The little robot in the corner is here whenever you need help.
learning.codeTitle: A little code. A real result.
learning.codeIntro: Pick a language, write something, and run it. Learn with examples or build your own idea.

tasks.0: Run a greeting, then change the message to your own name.
tasks.1: Use a function to calculate a result. Change the numbers and predict the answer.
tasks.2: Work with a list. Add a value and decide which results should appear.
tasks.3: Model a real task with structured code. Add one behavior and explain how it works.

webTasks.0: Make a heading and a paragraph. Change the words and the heading color.
webTasks.1: Create a card with HTML and CSS. Add another detail and adjust the spacing.
webTasks.2: Make a responsive grid. Add a card and compare different widths.
webTasks.3: Build a form with clear labels and keyboard focus. Try submitting it with an empty field.

learning.freeNote: This space is yours. Try a calculator, a small page, or any idea you like. Language changes keep a separate draft.
learning.runtimeLoading: Preparing the language for the first run…
learning.runError: The program stopped. Read the error or ask the helper.
learning.runnerUnavailable: This language’s runner is unavailable. Your code has been kept.
learning.stopped: Stopped. You can edit and run again.
learning.outputEmpty: Your program’s output will appear here.
learning.aiNotConfigured: Real AI review needs a provider connection. Built-in error guidance is available now.
learning.aiUnavailable: AI review is unavailable right now. Here is the built-in guidance.
learning.typoHelp: There may be a small spelling mistake in a command. Check {token}. You can review the suggested change and apply it, then run again.
learning.errorHelp: The checker reported an issue near line {line}: {message}. Check that line and the one before it, then run again.
learning.generalHelp: Try running the code first. Read the first error, check names and punctuation, and change one thing at a time. If it runs, change a value and predict the new result.
learning.privacy: Code runs in an isolated learning environment. Only asking the helper sends the current file and error to a configured AI provider. AI suggestions are untested until you run them.
learning.footer: Try it. Understand it. Make it work.
learning.previewReady: Your page is live. Edit the code and run again to refresh it.
